::: {.why}
Uniqueness, return magnitude and recency are three separate reasons to weight an observation, they interact, and applying all three without thinking is how a model ends up fitted to the last six months of large moves.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement sample weights combining uniqueness, absolute return attribution and time decay, each switchable.
- Report the effect of each weighting component separately on out-of-sample performance.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Implement the three weight components in qlib/ml/labels.py, each separately toggleable: uniqueness, the absolute return attributable to the observation over its label window, and an exponential time decay with a stated halflife. Multiply them and normalise.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Run the ablation rather than turning them all on: eight configurations across the three switches, evaluated under walk-forward with the effective sample size in the standard errors. Report which components help and by how much, and note that at least one probably does not. Log all eight.
:::
:::
